ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya and al-Zamakhsharī parse Ibrāhīm through coordination or an implied “remember”; the author objects that a past-time id is not a direct object here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: أو على الضمير في فأنجيناه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r3.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r3.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ḥanīfa, and Ibrāhīm read the name in the nominative: “and among the messengers was Abraham.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r3.anchor: وقرأ النخعي، وأبو جعفر، وأبو حنيفة، وإبراهيم: بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r4.claim: Abraham's story parallels Quraysh's situation and recalls their forefather's rejection of idols; Nimrod and his city worshipped idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r4.anchor: وهذه القصة تمثيل لقريش، وتذكير لحال أبيهم إبراهيم من رفض الأصنام

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r1.claim: Ibrahim is read in the accusative, the well-known reading, or in the nominative, meaning 'and among the messengers was Abraham.'
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r1.anchor: وفي إبراهيم وجهان من القراءة أحدهما : النصب وهو المشهور

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r2.claim: With the accusative, Ibrahim may be governed by an omitted 'remember,' or by the earlier 'We sent' in 29:14.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r2.anchor: أنه منصوب بفعل غير مذكور وهو معنى اذكر إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r3.claim: If 'when he said to his people' modifies 'We sent,' it seems to put the sending after the call even though sending normally precedes preaching; Razi offers two resolutions.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r3.anchor: أي أرسلنا إبراهيم إذ قال لقومه

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r4.claim: One resolution is that sending extends over time: Abraham remained a messenger while addressing his people, as standing can continue until a prince exits his house.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r4.anchor: أن الإرسال أمر يمتد فهو حال قوله لقومه اعبدوا الله كان مرسلا

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r5.claim: Alternatively, Abraham already recognized idolatry's error through God's guidance and called people to Islam before his formal sending; God sent him while he was preaching.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r5.anchor: هو أن إبراهيم بمجرد هداية الله إياه كان يعلم فساد قول المشركين

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r6.claim: One reading makes worship affirm God's existence and piety deny any other deity, since associating another with the sovereign is a grave offense.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى التوحيد لأن التوحيد إثبات الإله ونفي غيره

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r7.claim: Alternatively, worship means fulfilling obligations and fearing God means refraining from prohibitions; affirmation of God and avoiding shirk fall under these commands.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r7.anchor: الامتناع عن المحرمات ويدخل في الأول الاعتراف بالله

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r8.claim: Razi argues that reason requires a necessary existent as the cause of possible beings; denying God would leave existence without an ultimate cause and entail an impossible regress.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r8.anchor: أما عقلا فلأن الممكن لا بد له من مؤثر لا يكون ممكنا قطعا للتسلسل

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r9.claim: Associating partners with God is rationally impossible: a non-necessary partner cannot share God's status, while two necessary beings would be composite through shared and distinguishing attributes, so neither would be necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r9.anchor: وأما التشريك فبطلانه عقلا وكون خلافه خيرا وهو أن شريك الواجب إن لم يكن واجبا

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r10.claim: By social analogy, humans cannot own the heavens and earth; their highest rank is nearness to the sovereign, attained through worship and the prostration that draws one near.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r10.anchor: فأعلى درجاته أن يكون قريب الملك لكن القربة بالعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r11.claim: Razi supports nearness through worship with two quoted divine sayings: no approach surpasses fulfilling obligations, and a servant continues drawing near through worship.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r11.anchor: لا يزال العبد يتقرب بالعبادة إلي

RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r12.claim: The atheist has no rank because he denies any sovereign, while the idolater's master has inferior partners; one who affirms God's uniqueness therefore has the higher status, and worship and piety are best for those who understand the proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v25p39/r12.anchor: فإذن من يقول إن ربي لا يماثله شيء أعلى مرتبة ممن يقول سيدي صنم منحوت عاجز مثله

BURSEVI:v6p331/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331/r5.claim: Ibrahim is accusative by coordination with Noah; the implied command is to remember the time when Abraham spoke to his people.
BURSEVI:v6p331/r5.anchor: {وإبراهيم} نصب بالعطف على نوحا أي ولقد أرسلنا إبراهيم أيضا من قبل إرسالنا إياك يا محمد

BURSEVI:v6p331/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331/r6.claim: Abraham's people were the people of Babylon, including Nimrod.

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r1.claim: Abraham commands worship of God alone and warns them to fear Him by avoiding association with anything else.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r1.anchor: {اعبدوا الله} وحده {واتقوه} أن تشركوا به شيئا

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r2.claim: Worship and piety are better than their unbelief; the comparative wording accommodates their false belief, since unbelief contains no good at all.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r2.anchor: {ذالكم} أي ما ذكر من العبادة والتقوى {خير لكم} مما أنتم عليه من الكفر ومعنى التفضيل مع أنه لا خير فيه قطعا

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r3.claim: The condition means if they know and can distinguish good from evil.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r3.anchor: {إن كنتم تعلمون} أي : الخير والشر وتميزون أحدهما عن الآخر

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r1.claim: The Quran repeats Abraham’s story in over two hundred verses and presents Islam as a renewal of his creed, which Muslims are instructed to follow and invoke when defining their faith.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r1.anchor: Various aspects of Abraham’s story are repeated in over two hundred verses of the Quran. Islam presents itself as the renewal of his creed

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r2.claim: Abraham’s command to worship and reverence God summarizes his longer appeals in several other passages.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r2.anchor: The injunction to worship God and reverence Him is a summation of Abraham’s more extensive entreaties

TAB-FULL:v18p373/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p373/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to recall Abraham telling his people to worship God alone rather than idols, obey His duties and avoid sins; that is better for them if they can distinguish good from harm.
TAB-FULL:v18p373/r1.anchor: {واتقوه} [الأنعام: 72] يقول: واتقوا سخطه بأداء فرائضه، واجتناب معاصيه

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r9.claim: Abraham is grammatically coordinated with Noah, meaning that God also sent Abraham to his people.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r9.anchor: معطوف على قوله { نوحا } أي وأرسلنا إبراهيم إلى قومه

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r10.claim: In light of the following verses, Abraham's call to worship God and fear Him is a summons to monotheism and a warning, with worship restricted to God.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r10.anchor: دعوة إلى التوحيد وإنذار بقرينة الآيات التالية فتفيد الجملة فائدة الحصر

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r11.claim: Even without an explicit word of exclusivity, the command implies worship of God alone: idolaters worship intermediaries such as angels and jinn, believing God can only be approached through them.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r11.anchor: على أن الوثنية لا يعبدون الله سبحانه وإنما يعبدون غيره زعما منهم أنه تعالى لا يمكن أن يعبد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Abraham is conjoined to Noah, with an implied We sent: We also sent Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى: وأرسلنا إبراهيم، عطفا على نوح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as obey God and fear Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أطيعوا الله وخافوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r3.claim: Muqātil explains it as affirming God’s oneness and fearing Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r4.claim: Worshipping God is better for them than worshipping idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r4.anchor: {ذلكم} يعني: عبادة الله خير لكم من عبادة الأوثان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī explains if you know as knowing that God is your Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إن كنتم تعلمون أن الله ربكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r1.claim: “And Abraham” means God sent Abraham to his people and continues the preceding account of Noah being sent to his people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإبراهيم} [العنكبوت: 16] ، أي: وأرسلنا إبراهيم إلى قومه، وهذا تبع للكلام الأول لقوله في نوح: {ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه} [العنكبوت: 14]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r2.claim: Abraham’s command to worship God means affirm God’s oneness.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r2.anchor: قال: {إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله} [العنكبوت: 16] ، يعني: وحدوا الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains “fear Him” as fearing God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.claim: Abraham called his people to worship the one God, a principle shared by all prophets, reflect on whether idols truly have divine qualities, and learn from earlier peoples who called their messengers liars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.anchor: İbrâhim, öncelikle halkını, bütün peygamberlerin tebliğlerinin ortak ilkesi olan bir Allah’a kul olmaya, tanrı diye taptıkları putların gerçekten tanrı niteliklerine sahip olup olmadıkları üzerinde düşünmeye çağırmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r2.claim: Worshipping and obeying God benefits people themselves: serving others damages human dignity and personality, while disbelief prevents salvation in the hereafter and ultimately harms worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r2.anchor: İnsanın Allah’a kul olup O’na saygıyla itaat etmesinin faydası yine insanın kendisinedir

NAHHAS:v3p252/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm is accusative, coordinated with the object pronoun in the preceding verb.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r2.anchor: منصوب بأنجينا بعني أنه معطوف على الهاء

NAHHAS:v3p252/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r3.claim: A second possible parse coordinates Ibrāhīm with Noah, giving the sense We sent Ibrāhīm.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r3.anchor: وأجاز أن يكون معطوفا على نوح والمعنى وأرسلنا إبراهيم

NAHHAS:v3p252/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r4.claim: A third possible parse makes Ibrāhīm accusative under an implied command: Remember Ibrāhīm.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r4.anchor: وقول ثالث أن يكون منصوبا بمعنى واذكر إبراهيم

SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r1.claim: The common accusative coordinates إبراهيم with نوحا, supplies اذكر, or coordinates with the pronoun in أنجيناه.
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r1.anchor: العامة على نصبه عطفا على " نوحا " ، أو بإضمار اذكر، أو عطفا على هاء " أنجيناه ".

SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r2.speaker: النخعي وأبو جعفر وأبو حنيفة
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r2.claim: Al-Nakha'i, Abu Ja'far, and Abu Hanifa read إبراهيم nominative as subject with omitted predicate ومن المرسلين إبراهيم.
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r2.anchor: والنخعي وأبو جعفر وأبو حنيفة " وإبراهيم رفعا على الابتداء، والخبر مقدر أي: ومن المرسلين إبراهيم.

SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r3.claim: إذ قال is a badal of inclusion from إبراهيم.
SAMIN-DURR:29:16/r3.anchor: قوله: " إذ قال " بدل من " إبراهيم " بدل اشتمال.

ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r3.claim: The sense is We sent Abraham, conjoined with Noah's account.
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r3.anchor: المعنى وأرسلنا إبراهيم عطفا على نوح

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r1.claim: Alusi parses إبراهيم as accusative under an implicit اذكر, coordinating one story with the previous story despite their differing sentence forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r1.anchor: نصب باضمار اذكر معطوفا على ما قبله عطف القصة على القصة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya take إذ as an inclusion-substitute for إبراهيم; Abu Hayyan objects that إذ is indeclinable and cannot function as an object through substitution.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r2.anchor: وقد جوز الزمخشري وابن عطية وتعقب ذلك أبو حيان بأن إذ لا تتصرف فلا تكون مفعولا به

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan argues that past-time إذ cannot be governed by a command to remember, since a future act cannot occur in the past; it could be an object only if detached from its temporal use.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r3.anchor: أن إذ ان كانت ظرفا لما مضى لا يصح أن تكون معمولة لاذكر لأن المستقبل لا يقع في الماضي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r4.claim: Another parsing coordinates إبراهيم with نوحا to mean God sent Abraham; إذ then marks the sending, perhaps when Abraham had matured in reasoning and could guide others.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r4.anchor: وجوز غير واحد أن يكون نصبا بالعطف على نوحا فكأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r5.claim: Some place Abraham's call before his formal mission as he neared adulthood; Alusi counters that the quoted statement in 29:18, if spoken by Abraham, indicates he had already been sent, while a note by al-Sa'diyya says the verse need not imply formal mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r5.anchor: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول الا البلاغ المبين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa and Ibn Atiyya also allow إبراهيم to coordinate with the object of نجيناه, but Alusi calls that parsing poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r6.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء وابن عطية أن يكون نصبا بالعطف على مفعول انجيناه وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r7.claim: Alusi prefers coordination with نوحا, supported by the later parallel wording about sending Shuayb to Midian.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r7.anchor: أن يكون النصب بالعطف على نوحا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة والنخعي وأبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa, al-Nakha'i, and Abu Ja'far read إبراهيم in the nominative, supplying a phrase such as among the messengers is Abraham.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة والنخعي وأبو جعفر وإبراهيم بالرفع على أن التقدير ومن المرسلين إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r9.claim: Other proposed estimates for the nominative are among what ought to be mentioned or among those saved; Alusi prefers the first estimate because the surrounding verses support it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r9.anchor: وعلى الاول المعول لدلالة ما قبل وما بعد عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r10.claim: Abraham calls them to worship God alone and fear associating anything with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r10.anchor: اعبدوا الله وحده ( واتقوه أن تشركوا به سبحانه شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r11.claim: The worship and piety are better either than everything beneficial or than the people's present practice, assuming they regard that practice as beneficial; خير may mean good rather than comparative better.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p143#3/r11.anchor: ذلكم أي ما ذكر من العبادة والتقوى خير لكم من كل شيء فيه خيرية أو مما أنتم عليه على تقدير الخيرية فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144/r1.claim: If they can distinguish good from evil, they can recognize this worship and piety as better; even knowing anything at all is enough to judge it so.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144/r1.anchor: أي الخير والشر وتميزون أحدهما من الآخر أو أن كنتم تعلمون شيئا من الأشياء بوجه من الوجوه فان ذلك كاف في الحكم بخيرية ما ذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#2/r5.claim: “And Abraham” means that God sent Abraham; he told his people to obey and fear God, which is better for them if they know.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#2/r5.anchor: {وإبراهيم} أي: وأرسلنا إبراهيم، {إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه}

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r1.claim: إبراهيم may be coordinated with Noah, be an object of an implied اذكر, or be nominative with an implied ومن المرسلين إبراهيم.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r1.anchor: عطف على { نوحا } أو نصب بإضمار اذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r2.claim: إذ is attached to أرسلنا: Abraham was sent when his judgment matured and he recognized the truth; alternatively it is an appositional substitute if اذكر is understood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r2.anchor: ظرف لأرسلنا أي أرسلناه حين كمل عقله وتم نظره بحيث عرف الحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r3.claim: Abraham told his people to worship God and fear Him because that is better than their current practice, if they can distinguish good from evil or reason with knowledge rather than ignorance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r3.anchor: الخير والشر وتميزون ما هو خير مما هو شر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r7.claim: The preferred construction is We sent Abraham, parallel to the account of those sent to Midian; the alternative is an imperative to remember Abraham as an exemplary forefather for the Prophet and a lesson for his people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : واذكر إبراهيم أباك العظم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r8.claim: An alternative construes the opening as Remember Abraham, the great forefather, so the Prophet may follow and take comfort from him and his people may learn from his story.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : واذكر إبراهيم أباك العظم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r9.claim: On the Remember Abraham construction, إذ is an appositive of inclusion, since the narrated occasion contains the person remembered.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r11.claim: Abraham commands worship of God as He directs and fear of Him by avoiding any association, lest He punish them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r11.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم بما يأمركم به من طاعته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r12.claim: Exclusive worship and reverent fear of God are better for them than anything.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r12.anchor: ذلكم } أي الأمر العظيم الذي هو إخلاصكم في عبادتكم له وتقواكم { خير لكم } أي من كل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r13.claim: The conditional rebukes them: if they count as rational beings rather than brute animals, they should recognize this good; animals pursue what benefits them, so people who do not are worse.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r13.anchor: إن كنتم } أي بما لكم من الغرائز الصالحة { تعلمون * } أي إن كنتم في عداد الحيوانات العجم , بل أضل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Abraham grew unusually quickly, with each day like a week and each week like a month, then grew up and went to call his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي قال : ولد ابراهيم عليه السلام فكان في كل يوم مر به كانه جمعة والجمعة كالشهر من سرعة شبابه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses خير لكم as أفضل لكم, meaning better or more excellent for you.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : خير لكم يعني : افضل لكم .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.claim: “Ibrahim” may coordinate with Nuh, with the pronoun in “We saved him” (29:15), or depend on an implied “remember Ibrahim.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون إبراهيم معطوفا على «نوح»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.claim: The story is also an illustrative parallel for Quraysh.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.claim: Nimrod and the people of his city worshiped idols; Abraham called them to God's oneness and worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.anchor: وكان نمرود وأهل مدينته عبدة أصنام فدعاهم إبراهيم إلى توحيد الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Ibrahim is coordinated with Noah, meaning ‘We sent Ibrahim.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج هو معطوف على نوح والمعنى أرسلنا إبراهيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r2.claim: Worship of God is better than idol worship for those who know good from bad, though the people do not know.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p263#2/r2.anchor: يعني عبادة الله خير لكم من عبادة الأوثان إن كنتم تعلمون ما هو خير لكم مما هو شر لكم والمعنى ولكنكم لا تعلمون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.claim: Abraham, the exemplar of the hanifs, calls his people to worship God alone, fear Him, seek provision only from Him, and thank Him as the sole giver of blessings; this brings good and repels harm in both lives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.anchor: دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، والإخلاص له في التقوى، وطلب الرزق منه وحده لا شريك له، وتوحيده في الشكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r2.claim: The command means sincere worship and fear of God; doing so is better for them if they know, earning good and averting evil in both lives.

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r5.claim: Abraham tells his people to worship God and fear Him, since that is better for them if they understand.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r5.anchor: إبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r13.claim: Ibrahim is either coordinated with Nuh, implying “We sent,” or governed by an omitted “Remember Ibrahim.”
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r13.anchor: نصب (إبراهيم) قيل: عطفا على (نوح) أي: أرسلنا إبراهيم، وقيل: نصب بمحذوف، أي: اذكر إبراهيم.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm may be accusative through an implied اذكر, with إذ قال as a بدل اشتمال because the time includes what occurred in it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r1.anchor: نصب { إبراهيم } بإضمار اذكر ، وأبدل عنه { إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r2.claim: Alternatively, Ibrāhīm is coordinated with Nūḥan, and إذ marks when God sent him, once his age and knowledge enabled him to counsel his people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r2.anchor: أو هو معطوف على { نوحا } وإذ ظرف لأرسلنا ، يعني : أرسلناه حين بلغ من السن والعلم مبلغا صلح فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa read إبراهيم in the nominative, meaning that Abraham too was among the messengers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r3.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة رحمهما الله . ( وإبراهيم ) ، بالرفع على معنى : ومن المرسلين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r4.claim: The condition means either knowing what benefits or harms, or looking with discerning insight instead of blind ignorance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r4.anchor: يعني : إن كان فيكم علم بما هو خير لكم مما هو شر لكم . أو إن نظرتم بعين الدراية المبصرة دون عين الجهل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r13.claim: The verses through the account’s endpoint at 27:56 may continue Abraham’s speech, or may be an aside about Muhammad and Quraysh within Abraham’s story.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r13.anchor: وهذه الآية والآيات التي بعدها إلى قوله : { فما كان جواب قومه } ( النمل : 56 ) محتملة أن تكون

MUQATIL:29:16-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r1.claim: Abraham’s command to worship God means affirm His oneness; fear Him means fear God, which is better than worshipping idols.
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r1.anchor: يعنى وحدوا الله، { واتقوه } ، يعنى واخشوه

MUQATIL:29:16-17/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r2.claim: The qualification means that this is better if they know, although in fact they do not know.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r1.claim: Ibrahim may be accusative after an implied adhkur, with إذ قال as a genitive apposition of inclusion; it may instead coordinate with Noah or be a time adverb for God's sending him when he was ready to preach.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, إذ قال is a time adverb for 'We sent him': Ibrahim was sent when his age or knowledge qualified him to exhort his people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r2.anchor: أو ظرف لأرسلنا يعني أرسلناه حين بلغ من السن أو العلم مبلغا صلح فيه لأن يعظ قومه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and Abu Hanifa read Ibrahim in the nominative, meaning 'and among the messengers was Ibrahim.'
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة رضي الله عنهما إبراهيم بالرفع على معنى ومن المرسلين إبراهيم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r4.claim: Worship and fear God; doing so is better for you than unbelief, if you know what benefits and harms you.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#4/r4.anchor: إن كان لكم علم بما هو خير لكم مما هو شر لكم

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r1.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r1.claim: Al-Kisaʾi parses Ibrāhīm as accusative governed by anja(y)nâ, coordinated with the pronoun in “We saved”.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r1.anchor: قال الكسائي: { وإبراهيم } منصوب ب { أنجينا } يعني أنه معطوف على الهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r2.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r2.claim: Al-Kisaʾi also allows coordination with Nuh, yielding “and We sent Abraham”.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r2.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي أن يكون معطوفا على نوح، والمعنى وأرسلنا إبراهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r3.claim: A third parsing makes Ibrāhīm accusative under an implied “remember”.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r3.anchor: وقول ثالث: أن يكون منصوبا بمعنى واذكر إبراهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r4.claim: Abraham tells his people to worship God alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r5.claim: He tells them to fear God’s punishment and torment.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r6.claim: Worshipping God and fearing Him is better than worshipping idols, if they know.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r6.anchor: أي من عبادة الأوثان { إن كنتم تعلمون }

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r1.claim: As with Noah, Abraham was sent as a messenger to call his people to worship God and fear His wrath; the warning is timely counsel for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r1.anchor: just as God sent Noah (sws) to his nation as a messenger, similarly He also sent Abraham (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r2.claim: “Fear God” means avoiding His wrath by not associating partners with Him in worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p23/r2.anchor: means fear God ie. do not invite His wrath by associating partners with Him in worshipping Him.
